subject: Service assurance annualization, escalation matrix & pricing clarification
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@acme.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acme.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Service assurance annualization, escalation matrix & pricing clarification

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the time on Wednesday. I've attached an updated proposal (v3) and an escalation matrix workbook that maps response tiers to named contacts and oncall windows. A few clarifying items you asked for during the call:

- Annualization / billing cadence: we showed a 12-month commitment in the doc. We can also offer a monthly-billed variant with the same SLA bands but a smaller up-front discount.
- Oncall retainer: the proposal shows a 40-hour/month retainer for Priority+ customers with 24/7 escalation routing. We can scale to 80 hours/month at a different price point — see the redlined table in the PDF.
- Volume hurdle discounts: we've attached a schedule — once token usage exceeds 3x baseline for a consecutive month, the customer unlocks an incremental 10% credit on the monthly support line (does not affect per-token consumption pricing).
- Incident credits: formula is uptime-based (per-month SLA credits) and an additional operational credit if escalation response misses the response SLA twice in a rolling quarter.

Could you confirm which billing cadence Acme prefers (annual vs monthly) and whether the procurement team needs separate line-item pricing for the retainer vs hourly overage? If helpful, I can push a DocuSign request once we lock terms.

Attachments: Redwood_Service_Assurance_Proposal_v3.pdf (proposal), SLA-escalation-matrix.xlsx (matrix workbook)

Thanks —
Jordan
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service assurance annualization, escalation matrix & pricing clarification

Jordan — quick note from pricing:

- If Acme goes annual commit, we can move the retainer effective discount from 12% to 18% on the support line and include a one-time onboarding credit equal to one month of retainer.
- For monthly billing, suggest keeping the retainer at list price but offer a tiered volume credit schedule: 3-5x baseline = 5% credit, 5-10x = 12% credit, >10x = 20% credit. Credits apply to the support/retainer line only.
- Escalation matrix add-on: we can offer a named-engineer SLA (2-hour response, 24/7) as an optional bolt-on at $9k/mo.

If procurement pushes back, recommend we trade the named-engineer bolt-on for a limited 6-month price protection guarantee. That seems to be a low-risk concession.

—Karthik
Head of Deal Structuring
From: Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@acme.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 08:48:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Service assurance annualization, escalation matrix & pricing clarification

Jordan — thanks for the materials, and thanks Karthik for the options. A few follow-ups from procurement: 

1) Can you separate the price table into three line items: support retainer, named-engineer bolt-on, and per-token overage? Procurement wants independent numbers for each so they can feed into their MSA.
2) For annual commit: what's the penalty if Acme reduces committed usage mid-year? Is there a true-up or an early termination calculation? Please add a short paragraph in the proposal around mid-term true-ups.
3) The escalation matrix looks good, but the procurement lawyer asked whether Redwood will include a 4-hour summary report after Severity 1 incidents. Is that something you can commit to?

Preference: Acme is leaning to annual billing for predictability, but they want the mid-term true-up language clarified first. If you can provide the separated line-item PDF and add the true-up language, we can move to approvals.

Sam
VP, Cloud Platform — Acme Corp
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@acme.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service assurance annualization, escalation matrix & pricing clarification

Sam — happy to confirm operations-side items: 

- 4-hour incident summary: we can commit to producing an initial incident summary within 4 hours for Severity 1 events. The full post-incident report will follow our standard 72-hour cadence.
- Mid-term true-ups: we do a quarterly reconciliation for annual contracts; if committed usage falls short by >25% for two consecutive quarters, a pro-rata true-up applies for the shortfall or Acme can elect to reduce the commit with a 60-day notice and a 2% wind-down fee. We will draft the language for the proposal.
- Named-engineer: we'll make the on-call roster visible in the escalation workbook and allow one shadow substitution per 6-month period.

I'll work with legal to get the exact MSA-friendly phrasing and send an updated proposal with separated line-items and the true-up paragraph by EOD Friday.

—Grace
Head of Customer Reliability Operations
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@acme.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service assurance annualization, escalation matrix & pricing clarification

Sam —

Thanks for the clear guidance. Action items and next steps: 

1) We will send an updated, separated-line-item PDF that splits support retainer, named-engineer bolt-on, and per-token overage. Expect that in your inbox tomorrow morning. (Attachment: Redwood_Service_Assurance_Proposal_v3-lineitems.pdf)
2) Grace will provide MSA-ready true-up language and the 4-hour incident summary commitment; legal will bake that into the DocuSign packet.
3) Karthik: price structure for annual commit will be 18% discount on support retainer + onboarding credit (as discussed). If procurement wants monthly billing, we'll default to the monthly credits schedule.
4) Once procurement confirms the line-item PDF and the true-up language, Jordan will issue the DocuSign and propose a signature deadline of 2027-08-02 to preserve pricing.

Sam — appreciate the progress. If there's any internal stakeholder you'd like pulled into the next call (legal/IT security), I can schedule a 30-minute touchpoint.

Best,
Jordan
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
